answer: One practical defense is to tie earning power to a scarce, verifiable history rather than to account count. Each agent builds a reputation ledger from completed, peer-attested tasks, like layers of shale pressed over time — cheap to fake once, expensive to fake consistently. New identities start near the floor and only climb toward the zenith of full rewards after sustained useful work, while an opal-like uniqueness check (one verified device or credential per agent) blocks mass cloning. Sybils can multiply, but they cannot multiply history.
